name: Accenture
summary: For freshers in India, candidates commonly report online cognitive, technical and coding assessments and a spoken-English communication test, followed by one interview that mixes technical and HR questions. Accenture says its technical assessments evaluate problem-solving, logical reasoning and applied technical knowledge, and it publishes six core values, from Client Value Creation to Stewardship. Outside India, candidates usually report a recruiter screen and team interviews instead.

covers: Your studies or work so far and your strongest skills
One project or experience that shows how you work with others
Why this role at Accenture is your next step, in under two minutes

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked in a team to meet a deadline.
covers: The deadline, what was at stake and what made it tight
Your own part: what you took on and how you kept others in step
Whether you made it, and what you'd plan differently next time

questions.text: What do you know about Accenture?
covers: What it does in a sentence: consulting, technology and operations services for clients
One recent piece of work or news in the area you're applying for
Why that makes you want to work there

questions.text: How do you keep learning new technologies?
covers: Your actual routine: courses, documentation, side projects, certifications
One recent example of something you learned and used
How you decide what's worth learning next

questions.text: Tell me about a time a plan changed suddenly and you had to adapt.
covers: What changed and why it mattered
How quickly you adjusted and what you dropped or re-planned
The result and what it taught you about handling change

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped someone from a different background feel included in a team.
covers: Who they were and why they were on the edge of the group
What you did, such as changing how meetings ran or pairing with them
How the team and their work changed afterwards

questions.text: Tell me about a time you did more than you were asked to make a customer or user happy.
covers: What they asked for and what they really needed
The extra step you took and why it was worth it
How you know it made a difference to them

questions.text: Explain cloud computing to a client who has never used it, and name one risk they should know about.
covers: A plain-words explanation: renting computing power and storage instead of owning servers
The main benefits: paying for what you use, scaling up and down, less maintenance
One honest risk, such as cost control, security settings or dependence on one provider

questions.text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases, and when would you choose each?
covers: SQL: tables, fixed schema, joins and strong consistency
NoSQL: documents, key-value or other models, flexible schema, easier to spread across servers
An example for each, such as banking records versus a product catalogue

questions.text: A client says their shopping website is down during a big sale. What are your first steps?
covers: Confirming the problem and how many users it affects
Getting the site back first (roll back a release, add capacity) before the full root cause
Keeping the client updated regularly, then a review of what caused it

questions.text: How would you estimate how many people in Bengaluru order food through an app in a week?
covers: A clear structure: population, share with smartphones, share who order online
Sensible assumptions for how often each group orders, stated aloud
A final number with a quick sanity check against something you know

questions.text: For experienced candidates: tell me about a project where you moved a client's system to the cloud or a new platform. What went wrong?
covers: The starting point, the target and why the client wanted the move
Your role and the problem that surprised the team
How it was fixed and what you'd plan differently on the next migration

questions.text: Why do you want to work in consulting and technology services rather than at a product company?
covers: What appeals about working for different clients and industries
The skills you expect to build faster that way
An honest view of the trade-off, such as less ownership of one product

questions.text: Do you have any questions for us?
covers: One or two thoughtful questions about the team, first projects or learning support
Nothing already answered on the careers site
A brief thank-you

tips: Speak clearly and at an even pace: there's a separate spoken-English test.
Read Accenture's recent work in your area before the interview.
In the communication test, listen to the whole prompt before answering and keep your sentences short and complete.
Practise coding problems under time in the language you'll choose, including reading input and printing output correctly.
Prepare stories on teamwork, deadlines and adapting to change; the single interview mixes them with technical questions.

sources.title: Accenture Code of Business Ethics, with its core values (accenture.com)

rounds: Online application, with a short assessment for some roles
Interviews with the team: technical or case questions alongside behavioral ones
Final interview with a manager or senior leader
tips: Have stories ready about working with clients and in teams under deadlines.
Read Accenture's recent work in your area before the interview.
Prepare a story about adapting to change and one about including others; Accenture lists Respect for the Individual and Best People among its core values.
If you get an online assessment, expect problem-solving and logical reasoning; Accenture says it looks at how you approach the problem, not only the answer.
